11 A satellite uses two thrusters to adjust its motion in space.
Each thruster exerts a force of 40 N on the satellite. The line of action of each force is a
perpendicular distance of 2.3 m from the centre of gravity of the satellite. These two parallel
forces act in opposite directions.

hints: Notice the two $40\text{ N}$ arrows point in opposite directions, one up on the left and one down on the right, each $2.3\text{ m}$ from the centre line.
Recall that torque about the centre is $F \times d$ for each force, and the two turns act in the same rotational sense to form a couple.
Check the vector sum of $40\text{ N}$ up plus $40\text{ N}$ down for the resultant force, and add both $40\text{ N} \times 2.3\text{ m}$ moments for the total torque.
walkthrough: Identify the couple: left thruster pushes $40\text{ N}$ up $2.3\text{ m}$ left of centre, right thruster pushes $40\text{ N}$ down $2.3\text{ m}$ right of centre.
State the rules: resultant force is the vector sum $F_{net} = F_1 + F_2$, and each torque magnitude is $\text{torque} = F \times \text{perpendicular distance}$.
Find resultant force: $+40\text{ N}$ and $-40\text{ N}$ in the same line direction cancel, so $F_{net} = 40 - 40 = 0\text{ N}$.
Find total torque: both forces tend to turn the satellite the same way, so add moments: $40 \times 2.3 + 40 \times 2.3 = 92 + 92 = 184\text{ N m}$.
Check units and options: torque is in $\text{N m}$ and to two significant figures $184\text{ N m}$ is $180\text{ N m}$, with $0\text{ N}$ resultant force. This is option C.

A.explanation: This uses only one $40\text{ N}$ force times $2.3\text{ m}$. A couple needs the moment from both forces added together.

B.explanation: This uses only one moment of $92\text{ N m}$ and adds the $40\text{ N}$ magnitudes to $80\text{ N}$. Opposite directions cancel to zero resultant force.

C.explanation: Total torque is $2 \times 40\text{ N} \times 2.3\text{ m} = 184\text{ N m} \approx 180\text{ N m}$ and equal opposite forces give zero resultant force.

D.explanation: The torque of about $180\text{ N m}$ is correct, but the $40\text{ N}$ up and $40\text{ N}$ down forces cancel so resultant force is $0\text{ N}$, not $80\text{ N}$.
